claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
Last year's edition of this piece predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade, and the 2026 predictions held up.
AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner has forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027, and described cloud becoming a business necessity by 2028.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS posted $42.2 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, per Amazon's Q2 2026 results announcement.
AWS's Q2 2026 growth of 37% accelerated from 28% growth the prior quarter, and was its fastest revenue growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and its chips business (including custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, per Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 results (quarter ended June 30, 2026).
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
Hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030, per ResearchAndMarkets.
87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds, per Mordor Intelligence.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one.
Organizations must deploy workloads across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, on-prem, and edge while maintaining consistent security, compliance, and configuration, driven by AI and regulatory requirements.
According to McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report, cloud value driven by innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings.
According to McKinsey's report, high-performing organizations can achieve EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030.
According to McKinsey's report, Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.
According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending, spanning software, hardware, and services, is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Enterprises are investing in GPU provisioning and orchestration, data pipelines, vector databases, feature stores, and LLM infrastructure for real-time AI workloads.
Pulumi IaC integrates with third-party services including CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
Pulumi Policies helps teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates using AI-driven optimization.

Gartner predicts that by 2028, over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications, with total spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.

At the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney, Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said AI 'doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization.'
Pulumi ESC helps teams centralize and govern credentials, keys, and tokens.

According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team, and 35% are running a hybrid platform that combines existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: "Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale... What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications."
Large tech companies are the first adopters of platform engineering practices, and mid-size to large companies continue to invest in them.
Gartner predicts that agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts that human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 82% agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, yet manual approval remains close to universal today.
Pulumi's report describes the gap between trust in agents and real guardrails as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, the share of teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rises from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than faster dashboards and alerting alone.
AIOps includes observability, automation, and real-time analytics bridging DevOps, SRE, and IT operations.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
CNCF's Q3 2025 report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to the technology's growing maturity.

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, pushing organizations to schedule AI pipelines across edge and core clusters, often using Kubernetes as the common control plane.
Pulumi has published a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools at pulumi.com/blog/best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026/ and a post on Kubernetes AI platforms and policy convergence.
Kubernetes is evolving to support AI through GPU-aware scheduling and more advanced workload orchestration.
AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.

According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi Agent Skills is a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI, reducing hallucination and improving outputs.
Pulumi has a Remote MCP Server that provides infrastructure access to AI assistants, and Pulumi Neo executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Merging modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The post's title, meta description, and intro frame the trends as those shaping 2027 (title updated from 2026 edition).
